result:
The implementation is done. Summary of answers to your three questions:

**(1) Information missing or unclear:**
- Whether two unrefined `type X = Text` aliases (e.g. `ReportId` vs. a new `AdvanceId`) are nominally distinct or fully interchangeable. The task's own line — "audit entries for an advance use the advance's id in the *report* field" — only works if they're interchangeable, so I took that as confirmation and relied on it also for `Store.next_id()` and `Ledger.pay`'s `key` parameter.
- The exact tie-breaking rule when an advance's amount equals the report total exactly (does it count as "the advance covers the whole report" or "the report covered the advance"?). I resolved the boundary toward the "nothing paid, advance covers it" branch with `owed == 0`.
- Ordering of the two audit entries written by `pay_against` (report-paid vs. advance-settled) — spec doesn't say which comes first.

**(2) Part that caused the most unnecessary work:**
Making `audit.Entry.was`/`now` (and the query `Row.status`) hold either a `ReportStatus` or an `AdvanceStatus` required threading the "shared vocabulary" pattern (`ids.Step` + `audit.of_report`/`of_advance` converters) through every existing call site that built an audit entry for a report — six call sites across `review.brass` and `payment.brass` all had to be rewritten just to wrap existing values, even though none of their actual logic changed.

**(3) Assumptions made that the task didn't settle:**
- `AdvanceId` and `ReportId` are both plain `Text` aliases and interchangeable wherever `Text`/`ReportId` is expected.
- The advance-approval chain reuses `Requested` as the multi-step "awaiting approval" state (mirroring how reports use `Submitted`), since the spec lists only 4 advance states with no separate "under review" state.
- Advance approval's budget check uses the full `amount` (no budgeted/non-budgeted split, since advances have no line categories) — and conversely, report *and* advance approval budget checks now both include counted advances from the department/period via `budget.spend_of(reports, advances)`.
- `pay_against`'s reduced ledger payment uses the report's id as the ledger key (matching normal `pay`), not the advance's id.
- Kept all new orchestration logic inside existing modules (`review.brass`, `payment.brass`, `queries.brass`) rather than adding new modules, to stay at exactly 12 modules (the `impact_modules` limit) instead of exceeding it.
